A reproducible end-to-end workflow

Source: vignettes/end-to-end.Rmd
end-to-end.Rmd
library(vaxsurvR)

This vignette runs the whole pipeline on the synthetic example, in the order a real analysis would.

0. Describe the survey

Two objects, defined once, that everything else reads.

schedule   <- vcs_example_schedule
dictionary <- vcs_example_dictionary
schedule
#> <vcs_schedule: 14 dose(s), 7 antigen(s)>
#> # A tibble: 14 × 8
#>    vaccine antigen  dose label  minimum_age_days maximum_age_days previous_dose
#>    <chr>   <chr>   <int> <chr>             <dbl>            <dbl> <chr>        
#>  1 BCG     BCG         1 BCG                   0               28 NA           
#>  2 OPV0    OPV         0 OPV0                  0               14 NA           
#>  3 OPV1    OPV         1 OPV1                 42               76 OPV0         
#>  4 PENTA1  PENTA       1 PENTA1               42               76 NA           
#>  5 PCV1    PCV         1 PCV1                 42               76 NA           
#>  6 OPV2    OPV         2 OPV2                 70              104 OPV1         
#>  7 PENTA2  PENTA       2 PENTA2               70              104 PENTA1       
#>  8 PCV2    PCV         2 PCV2                 70              104 PCV1         
#>  9 OPV3    OPV         3 OPV3                 98              132 OPV2         
#> 10 PENTA3  PENTA       3 PENTA3               98              132 PENTA2       
#> 11 PCV3    PCV         3 PCV3                 98              132 PCV2         
#> 12 IPV1    IPV         1 IPV1                 98              132 NA           
#> 13 MCV1    MCV         1 MCV1                270              330 NA           
#> 14 YF      YF          1 YF                  270              330 NA           
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: minimum_interval_days <dbl>

1. Import 

raw <- vcs_example_raw
dim(raw)
#> [1] 600 216

In a real analysis this is read_vcs("survey.csv") or read_surveycto("export.csv").

2. Map 

mapped <- map_vcs_variables(raw, dictionary, schedule)
mapped
#> <vcs_data>
#>   households  : 600
#>   children    : 256
#>   vaccinations: 3584 rows (14 vaccine[s])
#>   raw import  : 600 x 216 (preserved)
#>   source      : NA

3. Validate 

qa <- validate_vcs(mapped)
summary(qa, by = "severity")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   group    severity n_issues n_records
#>   <chr>    <chr>       <int>     <int>
#> 1 CRITICAL CRITICAL       56        55
#> 2 ERROR    ERROR         350       304
#> 3 WARNING  WARNING       302       198
#> 4 INFO     INFO          103       103

Look at the critical issues before going further. In a scheduled pipeline this is where you would stop:

if (has_issues(qa, "CRITICAL")) {
  head(issues(qa, severity = "CRITICAL")[, c("rule_id", "record_id", "message")], 5)
}
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   rule_id       record_id   message                                             
#>   <chr>         <chr>       <chr>                                               
#> 1 ID_DUPLICATE  CH02731     "Identifier \"child_id\" is not unique."            
#> 2 ID_DUPLICATE  CH02731     "Identifier \"child_id\" is not unique."            
#> 3 DATE_PREBIRTH CH00121/BCG "Vaccination recorded 4 day(s) before the date of b…
#> 4 DATE_PREBIRTH CH00181/BCG "Vaccination recorded 1 day(s) before the date of b…
#> 5 DATE_PREBIRTH CH00301/BCG "Vaccination recorded 2 day(s) before the date of b…

4. Clean, flagging rather than correcting 

cleaned <- clean_vcs(mapped)
summary(cleaned$audit)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   rule_id           action severity n_records n_changes
#>   <chr>             <chr>  <chr>        <int>     <int>
#> 1 DATE_PREBIRTH     flag   CRITICAL        54        54
#> 2 CARD_DATE_NO_CARD flag   ERROR           17        17
#> 3 DATE_FUTURE       flag   ERROR            3         3
#> 4 DATE_UNPARSEABLE  flag   ERROR            2         2
#> 5 DATE_PARTIAL      flag   WARNING        104       104
log_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
export_cleaning_log(cleaned, log_file)

5. Derive the indicators 

d <- derive_vaccination_status(cleaned, evidence = "card_or_recall")
d <- derive_fully_vaccinated(d, vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA3", "MCV1"),
                             name = "basic_full")
d <- derive_zero_dose(d)
d <- derive_timeliness(d)

head(derivation_rules(d), 8)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   table    variable   rule                                                      
#>   <chr>    <chr>      <chr>                                                     
#> 1 children cov_BCG    vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 2 children cov_OPV0   vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 3 children cov_OPV1   vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 4 children cov_PENTA1 vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 5 children cov_PCV1   vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 6 children cov_OPV2   vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 7 children cov_PENTA2 vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…
#> 8 children cov_PCV2   vaccinated = card_or_recall (Documented on the card OR re…

6. De-identify 

salt <- "vignette-salt-not-for-production"   # in production: Sys.getenv("VAXSURVR_SALT")

anon <- deidentify_vcs(
  d,
  remove    = c("child_name", "caregiver_name", "telephone", "address"),
  hash      = c("child_id", "household_id"),
  salt      = salt,
  geography = list(lowest_level = "health_zone", round_gps = 2)
)
anon$deidentification$actions
#> [1] "removed direct identifiers: child_name, caregiver_name, telephone, address"
#> [2] "hashed identifiers (salted SHA-256): child_id, household_id"               
#> [3] "coarsened geography"                                                       
#> [4] "dropped the preserved raw import"
assess_reidentification_risk(anon)
#> <vcs_risk: k-anonymity screening>
#>   quasi-identifiers: province, district, health_zone, residence, stratum, sex
#>   records          : 256
#>   minimum k        : 1
#>   median k         : 5
#>   unique records   : 6 (2.3%)
#>   below k = 5      : 90 (35.2%)
#>   Consider generalize_geography() or generalize_age() before release.

7. Check the weights, then build the design 

issues(validate_weights(anon))
#> # A tibble: 30 × 8
#>    check            rule_id      severity level record_id variable value message

#>  1 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU001    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  2 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU002    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  3 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU003    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  4 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU004    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  5 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU005    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  6 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU006    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  7 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU007    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  8 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU008    weight   NA    Weight…
#>  9 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU009    weight   NA    Weight…
#> 10 validate_weights WT_VARIES_I… INFO     surv… PSU010    weight   NA    Weight…
#> # ℹ 20 more rows
design <- vcs_design(anon, ids = ~psu, strata = ~stratum, weights = ~weight)
design
#> <vcs_design>
#>   records : 256
#>   ids     : psu
#>   strata  : stratum
#>   weights : weight
#>   lonely PSU rule: adjust

8. Estimate

The standard presentation: each antigen by card, by recall, and by either source, with every child in every denominator.

by_evidence <- estimate_coverage_by_evidence(
  anon,
  vaccines    = c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA3", "MCV1"),
  design_args = list(ids = ~psu, strata = ~stratum, weights = ~weight)
)
by_evidence[, c("indicator", "evidence", "numerator", "denominator",
                "estimate", "conf_low", "conf_high")]
#> <vcs_estimate: 12 row(s)>

#> [4] "date_completeness.csv" "quality.csv"           "structure.csv"

What makes this reproducible

  • The schedule and dictionary are data, so the same script runs against next round’s export without editing any function.
  • The raw import is preserved through mapping, so any derived value can be traced to its source.
  • derivation_rules() states every definition applied.
  • audit_changes() states every value touched.
  • The evidence definition, the fully-vaccinated dose set, the zero-dose marker and the dropout method are all explicit arguments that appear in the script and in the output metadata.
  • The de-identification record lists what was done without ever containing the salt.

Run the script twice, and you get the same numbers. Hand it to a colleague with the salt, and they get the same numbers. Hand it to a reviewer without the salt, and they can still read every decision you made.
